solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Admit idling for a change; that's pretty average

indicators.note: a change made to the words before it means their letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admits they have been slacking, which is a fairly ordinary thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' looks like part of the phrase 'for a change', but it is anagram fodder; 'a change' is the signal. Every letter of ADMIT IDLING FOR is used.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom for something that is middling, neither good nor bad, just passable.

clue.text: Complaint by phone company, maintaining Czech Republic to a degree

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the phone company's letters hold the Czech code

parts.note: EE is a British mobile phone network
CZ is the international code for the Czech Republic
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A grievance about a phone company that keeps operating in the Czech Republic to some extent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grievance, but here it is a medical complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can mean an ailment, and this skin condition is one such illness.

clue.text: Star flower is found on end of sidewalk

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word sidewalk

explanation.surface: A star-shaped flower is growing at the edge of the pavement.
explanation.definitionFit: This printed symbol is the little star used to mark a footnote.

clue.text: Get two dinners delivered in London SW1

indicators.note: delivered suggests the letters are handed over in a new form, rearranged

explanation.surface: Ordering two takeaway dinners to an address in central London.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the Prime Minister's food order; the letters of GET TWO DINNERS are simply rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The street holding the Prime Minister's residence lies in the SW1 postal district of Westminster.

clue.text: Continue with summary

definitions.meaning: to carry on again after a pause
a short account of the main points, such as a CV

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means pick up again after stopping; as a noun, from French, it is a précis or CV.

clue.text: Glory that would be Greece with no end of cash

parts.note: GR is the abbreviation for Greece
with means and, joining things together

indicators.note: no end of means the last letter of the cash word is dropped

parts.note: the euro is the currency used in Greece

explanation.surface: Greece's former splendour would be gone without money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of' drops the last letter of EURO to give EUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Glory and this word are synonyms for magnificence or splendour.

clue.text: Ma isn't in Sacramento, but weirdly great-grandma is

indicators.note: isn't in means the letters of Ma are left out of the city's name
weirdly signals that the remaining letters are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: Mother doesn't live in the Californian capital, but strangely her grandmother does.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M and A from SACRAMENTO and rearrange the eight letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-grandmother is an example of a forebear from earlier generations of the family.

clue.text: Sadness as chap brought back tailless bird

parts.note: Reg is a man's name, a chap

indicators.note: brought back means the shortened bird is turned round
tailless means the last letter of the bird is cut off

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A man is sad because he returned with a bird that had lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' cuts TERN to TER, and 'brought back' turns that into RET.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadness over something done or lost is a close synonym for remorse or sorrow.

clue.text: Fearful blunders deceive a number outside

indicators.note: outside means the number goes round the other pieces

parts.note: ten is a number
blunders are errors
to trick someone is to deceive them

explanation.surface: Anxious mistakes fool a crowd standing outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fearful in the extreme is paralysed with fright, which this compound adjective describes.

clue.text: Swiss blend non-toxic but causes problems with vision

indicators.note: toxic suggests the letters have been poisoned and turned bad, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A harmless Swiss mixture nevertheless affects people's eyesight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-toxic' is split: NON belongs with SWISS BLEND as fodder and 'toxic' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Glare off snow can cause temporary sight loss, a condition of the eyes.

clue.text: Official found in Job Centre every day

indicators.note: found in means the answer sits within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A civil servant is at the employment office every day.
explanation.walkthrough: A Job Centre is the British state employment office.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a local administrative officer, such as a manor's steward or a town magistrate.

clue.text: No French participant is out of contention

definitions.note: describes a person or horse; the answer names one that is out of the running

parts.note: non is French for no
a runner is a participant in a race

explanation.surface: No French competitor has any chance of winning.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing, a horse withdrawn before the start cannot win, and figuratively anyone with no chance.

clue.text: Address refurbishment, having no time off

indicators.note: having no means the time-off word is removed from the refurbishment word

parts.note: restoration is refurbishment of a building
rest is time off work

explanation.surface: Tackle a renovation project without taking any breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' looks like a verb meaning tackle, but it is a noun: a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal speech given to an audience is a type of address.

clue.text: Towards what end does cab driver need such knowledge?

definitions.meaning: an old adverb asking for what purpose

definitions.text: does cab driver need such knowledge?
definitions.meaning: a taxi driver must know the destination the passenger asks for

explanation.definitionFit: It means to what purpose, and literally it is the cabbie's question about the destination.

clue.text: It's about bag of sweets, not that everyone would agree

definitions.meaning: a playful reading: liquorice allsorts are a British bag of mixed sweets
the saying that people differ in their tastes

explanation.surface: Commenting on a bag of sweets, conceding that not everybody likes it.
explanation.walkthrough: Liquorice allsorts are a British mixed sweet; the phrase is read as if it concerns them.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying shrugs that people vary widely, a comment on differing opinions and tastes.

clue.text: Box containing British Standard gets universal sign of approval

indicators.note: containing means the punch word holds the other pieces

parts.note: to box is to punch, to thump
BS is the abbreviation for British Standard
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: A packaging case meeting quality standards wins general approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a container but is the verb to punch. U is the British film certificate for all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising the thumb is a gesture showing approval or agreement.

clue.text: Shifty pros hide ball that's not completely round

indicators.note: shifty suggests the letters shift about into another order

explanation.surface: Crafty professionals hide a slightly misshapen ball.
explanation.definitionFit: This geometric solid is nearly a sphere but slightly flattened or elongated, like a rugby ball or the Earth.

clue.text: Date with stranger musician

parts.note: rummer means odder, stranger

explanation.surface: Going out with an unusual performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stranger' is the comparative of strange, not a person; RUM means odd in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussionist is one example of a musician in a band.

clue.text: Enid starts to follow, hand in glove

indicators.note: to follow means these letters come after the hand word

parts.note: mitt is slang for a hand
the starting letters of the name Enid

explanation.surface: Enid begins following someone, working in close partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hand in glove' suggests the idiom for close cooperation; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A glove without separate fingers is this kind, a warm winter covering for the hand.

clue.text: Japanese drama works without ending but is a total failure

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese masked drama

indicators.note: without ending means the last letter of the works word is dropped

parts.note: opera is the plural of opus, so works

explanation.surface: A Japanese play that never finishes is a complete flop.
explanation.walkthrough: OPERA, plural of Latin opus, means works; 'without ending' trims it to OPER.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for someone with no chance of success, a hopeless case.

clue.text: Support community stalwart

definitions.meaning: a column holding up a building
a dependable mainstay of a local group, as in the idiom about society

explanation.definitionFit: A column supports a structure, and figuratively a key member upholds a community.

clue.text: Halfway house is pretty within

indicators.note: within means these pieces go inside the house word

parts.note: an inn is a public house
be is the base form of is
twee means affectedly pretty or quaint

explanation.surface: A halfway house that is attractive inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Halfway house' reads as one phrase, but 'house' belongs to the wordplay. TWEE is British for sweetly quaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Something halfway sits in the middle, neither one thing nor the other.

clue.text: Reconcile Roger to having kept back a little souvenir

indicators.note: back means the held letters are read in the opposite direction
kept means the letters are held within the words Reconcile Roger

explanation.surface: Bring Roger round to holding on to a small keepsake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' hints that only a few letters of the phrase are used.
explanation.definitionFit: An object kept from the past as a memento is a keepsake of that kind.

clue.text: Judges fruit, so we're told

indicators.note: so we're told means the fruit word is heard rather than read

parts.note: gages are greengages, a type of plum

explanation.surface: Someone assesses fruit, according to hearsay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judges' looks like a noun but is a verb: estimates.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a quantity is to assess or measure it, a synonym in the verb sense.

clue.text: Determine new teatimes

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Fix new times for afternoon tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine an amount roughly is to calculate or assess it approximately.
